results.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
results.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

results.title: EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
results.content: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.

results.title: Why Iran's medicine supply chain is failing
results.content: Pharmacies in Iran are closing, hospital deliveries have stalled and patients are rationing doses or turning to black markets.

results.title: Is North Korea holding back on sending Russia more troops?
results.content: A North Korean troop buildup Ukraine warned about months ago has yet to materialize, even as strategic cooperation continues. Analysts say Pyongyang is balancing its ties with Moscow and Beijing.

results.title: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble
results.content: From Nvidia to Coreweave, AI and tech stocks have swung sharply in recent months. Some investors still see plenty of room to run, while others are trying to diversify — and finding it harder than expected.

results.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
results.content: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.

results.title: After Japan's APEC snub, what's next for its China ties?
results.content: Japan has long-running concerns over Chinese military expansionism, and Beijing has bristled at Sanae Takaichi's comments on Taiwan. The frosty ties were on full display at the APEC summit.

results.title: Nepal's new PM eyes closer ties with India amid lingering disputes
results.content: On his first foreign bilateral visit, rapper-turned-Prime Minister Balendra Shah sought deeper ties with Nepal's neighbor and largest trading partner, while steering clear of sticky territorial issues.

results.title: North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
results.content: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

results.title: Uganda minister at COP31: 'We need a just transition'
results.content: Funding from wealthy countries to help deal with the impacts of climate change hasn't materialized, says Uganda's environment minister. The East African country is hoping oil and carbon credits will help boost finances.

results.title: German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
results.content: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.
